Entries.Text: What the selected battle goal does: set the situation, see each act's chance of being picked, and click an act to watch its animations on the character.
The script has a syntax error; fix it to see its battle goal.
Not a battle goal: the script has no Goal.Activate.
Not a battle goal: no Goal.Activate in the script calls Common_Battle_Activate(ai, goal, weights, funcs, after[, params]).
Not a battle goal: no act is registered with REGIST_FUNC.
The character the battle goal runs on and the target it fights, shown in the Viewport window. Remembered per binder for this session.
The character the AI fights (TARGET_ENE_0): acts walk or run to it, turn to face it and attack toward it. Without one, an unseen target stands at the distance and bearing below.
Where the target stands, in degrees from the character's front (positive to its left), measured from where the character started.
Put the character back where it started, and the target at the distance and bearing.
Move the target with the viewport's translate gizmo.

Play: run the goal as the game does. Goal.Activate picks an act at random by weight, the act plays (its sub-goals, then the after function's), and when it ends the goal starts over with the situation as it now is. The distance to the target and the cooldowns come from the scene; move the target with the gizmo while it runs. Stop: back to the idle.
No act has any weight in this situation: waiting, then trying again.
While the simulation runs, this comes from the scene: the distance to the target, or whether the animation played within its cooldown.

What Goal.Activate's conditions read from the game, each its own input: numbers (distance, HP rate, random rolls), checkboxes (in front of the target, has a special effect, an animation still on cooldown) and choices (team role). Change them to see which acts the AI would pick. Click a name to show where the script reads it.
Put every input back to its starting value.
Goal.Activate's conditions read nothing from the game: the weights are always the same.

Animation {0} used in the last {1} s

Each act's chance of being picked in this situation (its weight's share of the total), and what it does at the current distance to the target. Click an act to play it on the character: its function runs with the situation, and each sub-goal that runs plays in turn (attacks, walking or running to the target, turning, strafing, backing off, waiting), then the character goes back to its idle. Double-click to show the act's function.
Click: play the act on the character. Double-click: show its function.
Act {0} does nothing the viewer can show in this situation (its sub-goals are on branches that don't run, or aren't ones it knows).
Skipped {0}: the character has no animation {1}

The NpcParam row the character runs as. Its ID gives the model; its animation offsets (its own, and its resident SpEffects') pick the clips it plays, and its behaviorVariationId picks its BehaviorParam rows.
Picking a battle goal picks the NpcParam row of an NpcThinkParam row that uses the goal, else the character's first row.

The NpcThinkParam row the goal reads its ai:GetExcelParam(AI_EXCEL_THINK_PARAM_TYPE__field) values from (thinkAttr_doAdmirer, caravanRole, weaponOnAnimId, …).
Any row can be picked: its battleGoalID is ignored, as the script selected is the battle goal simulated. Rows that run this goal are marked.
The NPC's own: the NpcThinkParam row of its NpcParam ID, else the first row that runs this battle goal

What ai:GetTeamOrder(ORDER_TYPE_Role) gives: the character's role in its team, which the game's team AI hands out.
Most battle goals (570 of ER's role checks) only use their attack weights for the attacker: with thinkAttr_doAdmirer set, a surrounder (ROLE_TYPE_Torimaki) strafes around the target and a spectator (ROLE_TYPE_Kankyaku) hangs back.
The character is its team's attacker (ROLE_TYPE_Attack), as a lone enemy is: it uses its attack acts
The character takes turns, as one of a group fighting the same target: the attacker for a while, then a surrounder (ROLE_TYPE_Torimaki) strafing around the target, and so on
The role is the Situation's GetTeamOrder input, yours to set
How long each turn as the attacker lasts
How long each turn as a surrounder lasts (0: always the attacker)

List only the rows of {0}, the character the battle script's filename names, and of its model variants ({1} to {2}), to switch between them without every other enemy listed.
The same setting for the NPC and Think lists. A row is a character's by its ID (43000000 is c4300's, 43010000 c4301's).
Filter by ID, name, chr ID or alias

Each clip plays at its ID plus the first of these offsets the character has a clip for, else at its own ID.
The resident SpEffects' offsets are tried before the row's animIdOffset2 and animIdOffset.

NpcParam normalChangeModelId shows another model, normalChangeAnimChrId plays another character's animations (and its TAE), normalChangeTexChrId wears another character's textures.
Swapped textures only show where their names match the model's materials, and only if they weren't loaded already.

NpcParam modelDispMask0..31: the mask groups shown (1); the rest are hidden, and a mesh without a group is always shown.
The playing clip's DrawMask events change them from their start, HideMask and ShowMask while they last.
Turn speed: none (faces the target at once)

NpcParam turnVellocity: how fast the character turns toward the target while it walks, runs, strafes, backs off, or turns on the spot without a turn clip.
During an attack clip it turns only while the clip's SetTurnSpeed events are active, at their speed (a negative one is taken as this speed). A clip without them faces the target as it starts.
NpcParam hitRadius: what ai:GetMapHitRadius(TARGET_SELF) gives. The scripts take it off their act distances (5 - radius), in Goal.Activate and in the act functions.
ai:HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_SELF, id) is true for these (NpcParam spEffectID0..31). Other SpEffects stay yours to set: events and the TAE give them.
Answered by the character: its NpcParam / NpcThinkParam rows, or a SpEffect its TAE has put on it (see Time Act)
while the event lasts, then {0} s
until the simulation is reset (effectEndurance below 0)

Put on by the TAE's AddSpEffect events: on while the event lasts, then for the SpEffect's effectEndurance.
The battle goal's HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_SELF, id) is true for them, so the next act is picked with them on.

Goal.Interrupt: what the goal does when something happens mid-act.
It runs by itself when the character's TAE puts on a SpEffect the goal observes on itself (INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect); fire the others by hand.
If it returns true, the act stops: what it queued plays instead, and the simulation picks again when that has played.
Run the Interrupt as if INTERUPT_{0} happened (tested at line {1})
Run the Interrupt as if SpEffect {0} had just gone on (INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect)
The act was interrupted (Goal.Interrupt took it)

The TAE events of the clip the character is playing, stepped with it.
Effect events spawn their FFX on their dummy poly; bullet events fire their Bullet row (through the character's BehaviorParam) at the target.
The TAE comes from the Time Act Editor (with any unsaved edits), the effects from the FX Editor's bank.
Show the effects that the TAE events and the bullets spawn (needs the FX Editor enabled for the project)
Fire the Bullet rows of the bullet events, flown by the Projectile Editor's simulation over flat ground, at the target
Log every event as it fires, not only the effects and bullets
TAE events need the Time Act Editor enabled for the project
No TAE entry for {0} in the character's anibnd (or the anibnds it shares)
Effects need the FX Editor enabled for the project
Loading effects: indexing the FX bank ({0} of {1} binders)
Loading effects: reading the character's TAE ({0} animations, {1} effects found)
{0}. The act starts when they are ready.

Every effect the character can trigger is made ready before an act plays: those of its TAE effect events in all its animations, and its bullets' flight and hit effects (child bullets too). Then none stalls when it first shows.
It starts when the character is picked, and again when what it animates with or the Viewport Filters' effect kinds change.
What the events did as they fired, newest first: scene time, clip, time in the clip, event, and what it spawned (or why it didn't)

Write the {0} Lua binders with unsaved changes into the project. Edited scripts are saved as text (the game loads text Lua), the binder's .luagnl is rebuilt, and every other entry keeps its bytes. A script with a syntax error isn't saved.
Switch the Script window between reading (coloured, Ctrl+click a name to go to its definition) and editing (a text box). An edit is applied when you leave the box; each applied edit is one undo step.
Show, after each binder, the NpcThinkParam rows whose logicId or battleGoalID is its number.

Give decompiled locals and arguments names worked out from their use (targetDist, ai, goal, actWeights, ...) instead of f2_local3. Applies to scripts decompiled after the change. The names don't change what the script does.
The project's Lua binders (.luabnd), by kind. Green: the project has its own copy.
The character this battle goal belongs to ({0}), from the first four digits of its goal ID
The project has its own copy of this binder.
NpcThinkParam rows using this goal ID (logicId or battleGoalID):
Become the target and fight the character yourself, in first person. The battle goal reads your distance and facing as it does a target moved with the gizmo, and your actions reach it as set below.

Walk on the flat ground the characters stand on, with the viewport movement keys and the Map Editor's first person keys. The target is placed at your feet, facing where you look, and hidden while you walk as it.
Walking as the target. {0} pauses (gives the mouse back).
Paused. Click in the viewport to carry on, {0} again to leave.
Puts you at the target's feet, looking at the character, with the mouse captured. {0} pauses, then leaves.
Move with the viewport movement keys, {0} to run, {1} to jump, {2} to roll, {3} for estus; left click attacks, right click (held) guards; {4} to pause.
Pick the character (NPC) first: there is no one to fight

How each of your actions reaches the AI: the interrupt it fires as it starts (Goal.Interrupt), and the SpEffects it puts on you for a while (HasSpecialEffectId(TARGET_ENE_0, id) sees them, and a goal that observes one on TARGET_ENE_0 gets INTERUPT_ActivateSpecialEffect).
Which SpEffect IDs mean rolling, drinking and so on is the project's data: set them here. Interrupt types the goal's Interrupt tests are marked.
Left click. Fires its interrupt (FindAttack: the AI sees you attack), and Damaged too when the character is within reach in front of you.
Right click, held. IsTargetGuard(TARGET_ENE_0) is true while held; its interrupt fires as the guard goes up, and its SpEffects stay on while held.
Drinks an estus flask: fires its interrupt (UseItem).
Rolls the way you move (or face), its distance over its time below.
Jumps, landing back on the ground.
How long the action's SpEffects stay on you
How long the guard's SpEffects stay on you after you let go
An attack also fires Damaged (the AI is hit) when the character stands within this distance, within 60 degrees of your front
How far an attack reaches, on the ground, from your feet to the character
SpEffect IDs, separated by commas, put on you as the action starts. Applied when you leave the field (Escape undoes).
{0} pause   LMB attack   RMB guard   {1} estus   {2} roll   {3} jump   {4} run
Paused: click to carry on, {0} to leave
What the viewport shows of the battle simulation. None of it changes the simulation: bullets still fly and hit, and the target is still where distances and aiming are measured from.
The effects drawn from the FX Editor's bank (the FX Editor has to be enabled for the project). One turned off goes at once; one that fires while it is off isn't shown when it is turned back on.
Play the effects at all: when off, none of the kinds below play
The effects the playing clip's TAE events spawn on their dummy polys
Each bullet's flight effect (its row's sfxId_Bullet), along its flight
Each bullet's hit effect (its row's sfxId_Hit), where it landed
The lines drawn over the viewport for the bullets in flight, as the Projectile Editor draws them
A sphere for each bullet in flight, its hit radius
A ring around each bullet in flight whose attack reaches further than the bullet itself (its AtkParam hit radius)
The path each bullet has flown
The reach of the attack, left for a moment where each bullet landed

Each clip crossfades from the one before, as in the game: the last clip plays on as it fades out, over the new clip's TAE Blend event, else the default below. Off, clips cut straight from one to the next.
How long a clip without a TAE Blend event (and the target's clips) blends in from the last
